label: lem:antideriv_diff_zero_deriv
title: Difference of antiderivatives has zero derivative
statement: Let $F$ and $G$ both be antiderivatives of $f$ on $\mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$ (i.e.\ $\texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn}\; F\; f\; a\; b$ and $\texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn}\; G\; f\; a\; b$). Then for every $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$, the function $F - G$ has derivative $0$ at $x$ (i.e.\ $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; (F - G)\; 0\; x$).
proof: For $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$, we have $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; F\; (f\;x)\; x$ and $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; G\; (f\;x)\; x$ by the antiderivative hypothesis. By \texttt{HasDerivAt.sub}, $F - G$ has derivative $f(x) - f(x) = 0$ at $x$.
